description: UPChallenge Team une el talento en tecnologías de la información de Chiapas con los datos abiertos de la NASA. En este Space Apps Challenge en Tuxtla, resolvemos el reto de las granjas creando software inteligente que ayuda a optimizar cultivos, gestionar recursos hídricos y anticipar riesgos climáticos.
summary:
K'INAL is an interactive AgTech MVP designed to democratize advanced agroclimatic intelligence for farmers across North America. By integrating real-time NASA satellite telemetry (POWER, SMAP, IMERG) with a custom XGBoost Machine Learning model, K'INAL accurately forecasts soil moisture reserves (GWETROOT) and calculates Growing Degree Days (GDD) for corn crops. To bridge the technical gap, we implemented a Gemini-powered RAG engine that translates complex meteorological data into plain-language, actionable agronomic advice. Built with a frictionless, globally scalable architecture, K'INAL helps farmers mitigate climate risks, avoid planting in non-viable zones, and optimize their crop cycles through an intuitive, map-driven dashboard.

Page for try:
https://nasa-space-app-challenge-farms-fron-kohl.vercel.app/
details:
What it does & How it works: K'INAL operates through an interactive map interface (Next.js/MapLibre). When a user clicks any coordinate in North America, the FastAPI backend fetches real-time telemetry from NASA APIs. A preflight viability check uses MODIS Land Cover and thermal data to discard non-arable lands (e.g., oceans or freezing zones). For viable lands, a trained XGBoost ML model (.joblib) calculates a 7-day soil moisture forecast. Finally, a Generative AI engine interprets these raw metrics to deliver localized agronomic recommendations.

Benefits & Impact: It translates elite, complex aerospace data into actionable farming advice. By providing localized drought warnings or frost alerts, K'INAL protects farmers from losing their seed investments, promoting food security and climate resilience.

Tools, Coding Languages & Hardware:

  • Frontend: Next.js (React), Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL JS, hosted on Vercel.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, hosted on Railway.
  • Machine Learning: XGBoost (Quantile Regression for p10/p50/p90 forecasts).
  • Generative AI: Google Gemini 2.0 Flash (via API) for text generation.
  • Hardware: Standard cloud compute (no specialized GPUs required for inference).

Creativity & Factors Considered: We prioritized UX and scalability. We bypassed traditional login barriers to create a "Frictionless Demo" and removed local geofences to ensure the ML pipeline could process requests continent-wide. We also implemented graceful degradation: if the AI detects a non-viable zone, it safely aborts predictive calculations and visually explains the environmental constraints to the user.
